The apply_template returned a tuple with one precursor: 'C=C(C)C(=O)O[C@@]1(C(F)(F)F)CCC[C@H]1C(=C)c1ccccc1'

That is a single molecule, not two. The retro template apparently splits into a carbonyl-alkene fragment but maybe the product is formed from a single precursor (intramolecular carbonyl-ene). Indeed carbonyl-ene can be intramolecular, so the precursor is a molecule containing both carbonyl and alkene in same chain that cyclizes to give product. So the retrosynthetic step is a single precursor (intramolecular). The route must have 1 reaction, which is fine: target -> precursor (single molecule). So we can present route with reaction children containing one precursor molecule.

We should verify that applying forward reaction (the reverse of retro) would give target. Use verify_step with template (forward direction). The template we have is retro_smarts; but verify_step expects retrosynthetic template (SMARTS) and precursors to produce target. We have template ID 1209837; we can use verify_step with target SMILES, template_id, precursors list containing the precursor SMILES.
Let's verify.
